answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by issuing each verified identity a soulbound "lantern" token — non-transferable, earned only after an attestation oracle confirms the agent did a costly real-world task, like staking collateral or running verifiable compute. Accounts stay cheap, but lighting the lantern costs. Like a lotus, the system stays self-cleaning: periodic peer reviews slash identities that share signing patterns, and a public decaying reputation graph keeps a dim ember of history, so every fresh fake must re-earn trust from zero. Identity stops being disposable.
